chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abī Jaʿfar, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليهما السلام, that he said:
"There is no harm in the droppings of chickens and pigeons getting onto the garment."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report does not contradict the report which we narrated before this from Fāris, from Ṣāḥib al-ʿAskar عليه السلام, that salat is not permissible in a garment touched by chicken droppings, because that report is to be understood as referring to the droppings of a jallāl chicken. But if it is not jallāl, then its ruling is the ruling of the rest of those whose meat is eaten, regarding the permissibility of salat with its droppings and urine.

key_terms.الْجَلَّالِ: an animal that habitually feeds on filth

ai.seo_question: Is salat valid in a garment affected by chicken or pigeon droppings?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the droppings of chickens and pigeons on a garment do not pose a problem. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī then reconciles it with another report by explaining that the contrary ruling concerns the jallāl chicken, while a non-jallāl chicken takes the ruling of animals whose meat is lawful to eat in the matter of salat.
